summary: Massachusetts-built steel lookout c.1915 on Berlin Mountain (Rensselaer Co., NY), moved to Brodie Mountain, Hancock, MA in late 1923; only footings remain on Berlin.

facts.status_note: Moved to Brodie Mountain in Hancock, Massachusetts, in late 1923; only the footings remain on Berlin Mountain. A 2026 guide describes a former tower with a cabin on East Mountain, Hancock, now out of service and carrying radio gear.

access.note: Much of the upper slopes and summit is protected conservation land, crossed by the Taconic Crest Trail

visit.trail_note: The 37-mile Taconic Crest Trail traverses the mountain; several other trails approach the summit from the east

events.note: Around 1915, Massachusetts built a 50-foot steel fire lookout tower; one of two built to replace the Mount Greylock tower
New York added forest fire observation stations at Number Seven Hill and Dickinson Hill, both in Rensselaer County
Massachusetts moved the tower to Brodie Mountain in Hancock in late 1923
Notice said a fifth tower, previously abandoned, atop Brodie Mountain in Hancock would return to service
1954 newspaper items say a tower at Brodie Mountain had been closed since before World War II; the closing date is not given
A 50-foot tower was built at Brodie Mountain
A new tubular steel tower was erected at Brodie Mountain

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1952 notice says a previously abandoned tower would return to service, and the 1954 items say a tower there had been closed since before World War II. The 2026 guide says the tower has kept watch since 1923. The record gives each claim with its date and does not choose one.

The Forest Lookouts page places the moved tower at Brodie Mountain, Hancock. The 2026 guide places the standing tower on East Mountain, about three miles south of Brodie's summit. Both are in Hancock, and the story names both.

notes_for_editor: Probable duplicate of us-ny-berlin-mountain: same Berlin Mountain lookout, same Wikipedia, Forest Lookouts and Brodie sources; merge candidate. This record's own source page (berlin-mountain1.html) has only the name and county, so the history comes from berlin-mountain.html, Wikipedia and the Brodie page. The brief's coordinates match Wikipedia's summit position, so no correction was made. The 1915 date rests on Wikipedia alone. No source says whether the 1923 structure survives on East Mountain beyond the 2026 guide.
